articles.title: 圆通回应“客户取消快递订单被记为投诉”事件：向客户道歉，不存在“咨询即处罚”“进线算投诉”情况
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，今晚，圆通速递就“客户取消快递订单被记为投诉”事件致歉。公告称，18 日晚，有媒体报道圆通一加盟网点“客户致电取消订单被登记为投诉？快递员上门称被罚款，孕妇受惊吓进医院”，并引发网络关注。圆通总部高度重视，第一时间进行调查核实。公司因此事对客户带来的身心不利影响真诚致歉。据悉，涉事加盟网点为浙江杭州市余杭区仁和网点，其在接到客户撤销寄件需求后，向当事快递员传导了错误信息，导致快递员误认为自己面临罚款，并在随后与客户沟通时情绪过激、言语不当。圆通表示将全力配合客户妥善处理后续相关事宜。IT之家附圆通速递原文如下：圆通回应“客户取消快递订单被记为投诉”事件：向客户道歉，不存在“咨询即处罚”“进线算投诉”情况，强化管理和培训18 日晚，有媒体报道圆通一加盟网点“客户致电取消订单被登记为投诉？快递员上门称被罚款，孕妇受惊吓进医院”，并引发网络关注。圆通总部高度重视，第一时间进行调查核实。公司因此事对客户带来的身心不利影响真诚致歉。经了解，涉事加盟网点为浙江杭州市余杭区仁和网点（下文简称“仁和网点”），其在接到客户撤销寄件需求后，向当事快递员传导了错误信息，导致快递员误认为自己面临罚款，并在随后与客户沟通时情绪过激、言语不当。圆通将全力配合客户妥善处理后续相关事宜。另外，此事件中，接受媒体采访的网点客服称“去咨询，就会变工单下来，对快递员有处罚”“进线就算投诉”“把单号告诉总部，就会变投诉”“…… 处罚 100 元一条”等，均不属实。公司已对快递员的不当言行进行批评教育，明确其培训合格后才能重新上岗，并调离原服务区域。同时，对浙江省区网管负责人进行处罚，对涉事加盟网点及相关客服人员进行通报批评并责令整改。目前，圆通对客户进线均由总部客服人员接待登记、分类处理。咨询类进线均不构成投诉。截至 10 月 19 日 19 时，此次事件中发生一项实际考核，原因是客诉工单处理超时，对网点客服人员的考核金额为 20 元，产生时间是 10 月 19 日 08:58:59。公司再次为此事对客户带来的身心不利影响深表歉意。同时，针对此事暴露出的省区和部分加盟网点管理缺位、一线人员业务能力不足、制度规则传导偏差等问题，我司将举一反三，持续强化整改、培训和管理，切实保障客户利益和一线员工合法权益。再次感谢媒体与社会公众的监督！（完）

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，谷歌研究人员近日发布论文称，他们使用四个 Gemini 4 Argon 智能体成功通关《我的世界》，仅用 27 小时就成功击败末影龙。谷歌将 4 个 Gemini 4 放入随机生成的世界中，他们可以通过游戏内的聊天框互相协调。但研究人员没有为他们制定任何策略，只是说了最终目标，所有行为都由智能体自行规划。研究人员可通过仪表板观察他们，下达暂停 / 终止测试指令，但没有权利介入。游戏开始后，这些智能体很快分担了不同任务：有的建造末影人农场；有的收集食物；有的专注于探索。它们会分享战斗技巧，并在队友死亡后寻回丢失的装备。整个游戏过程中，4 个智能体发送了 229 条消息、运行 2783 个程序，死亡 605 次。它们花了 13.5 小时才抵达末地，剩下的时间全部用来击败末影龙。整个过程用了 13.5 亿个输入 Token，按照普通用户标准来算，成本约为 1,620 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 10,842 元人民币）。研究团队表示：“据我们所知，这是 AI 智能体首次在完全自主的情况下从头到尾通关《我的世界》。整个过程仅使用标准的 Mineflayer 库，没有使用种子地图，也没有人类辅助。”

articles.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
articles.content: Google tried to overturn a landmark Munich ruling on AI search liability by appealing, then quietly settled. The strategy isn't working. The Aachen Regional Court just applied the exact same reasoning in a new case where Google's AI falsely attributed criminal offenses to a doctor that actually involved someone else. A consistent legal view is forming across German courts, and it treats Google's AI answers as the company's own content. articles.title: Tenstorrent 完成 15 亿美元 E 轮融资，投后估值 62 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，RISC-V AI 计算企业 Tenstorrent 美国当地时间今日宣布完成总额达 15 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 100.39 亿元人民币）的 E 轮融资。该企业投后估值达到 62 亿美元（现汇率约合 414.95 亿元人民币）。Tenstorrent 由知名芯片设计师 Jim Keller 领导，已发布过多款 AI 芯片产品。该企业此前在 2024 年底以约 27 亿美元的投后估值进行了 D 轮融资。该企业的 E 轮融资由 Trace Capital 和 Innovation X 领投，多家新老投资者参与其中。这笔资金将用于支持 Tenstorrent 的大规模量产和全球商业扩张。Jim Keller 表示：我们构建了一种统一的架构，并以各种规格进行销售，计算技术的未来是开放的、可扩展的，并且由在其上进行开发的人们所拥有。我们的投资者也认同这一模式，我们非常感谢他们的支持。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，微信开放平台与微信视频号团队今日联合宣布，发起「公众号小说改编微短剧：第一期」激励活动，支持原创小说开展改编短剧合作。首期选出 10 部深受微信用户喜爱的作品，平台已与作者确认改编意向。IT之家从“微信公开课”公众号获悉，短剧承制方与作者在活动有效期内达成合作，并按要求完成改编、在微信生态优先发行后，双方可各获改编短剧在微信生态优先发行期收入的额外 5% 现金激励，上不封顶。同时，激励对应的发行载体为绿泡泡短剧小程序、视频号端原生短剧，收入计算范围为短剧在微信生态优先发行前 30 天的变现收入。微信开放平台不占有小说的著作权及改编权。具体改编合作，由短剧承制方与作者协商一致并签署协议。此外，短剧承制方需与作者协商一致，共同签署改编协议，并以书面形式提交平台，支持短剧在微信生态优先发行。合同签署时间需在 2026 年 11 月 1 日至 12 月 31 日。改编短剧需在绿泡泡短剧小程序、视频号端原生短剧优先发行，发行前 30 天为微信生态优先发行期。

articles.title: 国家邮政局：1—9 月快递业务量累计完成 1513 亿件，同比增长 4.3%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，国家邮政局今日公布 2026 年 1-9 月邮政行业运行情况，IT之家整理主要内容如下：1—9 月，邮政行业业务收入（不包括邮政储蓄银行直接营业收入）累计完成 13893.1 亿元，同比增长 5.8%。其中，快递业务收入累计完成 11634.4 亿元，同比增长 7.2%。1—9 月，邮政行业寄递业务量累计完成 1641.3 亿件，同比增长 3.7%。其中，快递业务量累计完成 1513.0 亿件，同比增长 4.3%。9 月份，邮政行业业务收入完成 1588.6 亿元，同比增长 4.1%。其中，快递业务收入完成 1345.2 亿元，同比增长 5.6%。9 月份，邮政行业寄递业务量完成 186.6 亿件，同比增长 1.7%。其中，快递业务量完成 172.3 亿件，同比增长 2.1%。从业务类型看，1—9 月，同城快递业务量累计完成 110.0 亿件，同比下降 7.3%；异地快递业务量累计完成 1371.8 亿件，同比增长 5.4%；国际 / 港澳台快递业务量累计完成 31.2 亿件，同比增长 2.7%。1—9 月，邮政函件业务累计完成 6.1 亿件，同比增长 25.1%；包裹业务累计完成 2351.4 万件，同比增长 11.5%；报纸业务累计完成 117.6 亿份，同比下降 3.7%；杂志业务累计完成 4.2 亿份，同比下降 5.0%；汇兑业务累计完成 96.1 万笔，同比下降 34.8%。1—9 月，同城、异地、国际 / 港澳台快递业务量分别占全部快递业务量的 7.3%、90.7% 和 2.0%。与去年同期相比，同城快递业务量的比重下降 0.9 个百分点，异地快递业务量的比重上升 1.0 个百分点，国际 / 港澳台业务量的比重下降 0.1 个百分点。1—9 月，东、中、西部地区快递业务收入比重分别为 73.6%、15.6% 和 10.8%，快递业务量比重分别为 68.8%、20.8% 和 10.4%。与去年同期相比，东部地区快递业务收入比重下降 0.2 个百分点，快递业务量比重下降 2.3 个百分点；中部地区快递业务收入比重基本持平，快递业务量比重上升 1.2 个百分点；西部地区快递业务收入比重上升 0.2 个百分点，快递业务量比重上升 1.1 个百分点。1—9 月，快递业务收入品牌集中度指数 CR8 为 86.7，较 1—8 月下降 0.2；快递业务量品牌集中度指数 CR8 为 96.1，较 1—8 月下降 0.1。三季度，快递服务公众满意度得分为 85.3 分，全国重点地区快递服务 72 小时妥投率为 86.81%。

articles.title: 2026 年三季度印度智能手机市场遇冷，iPhone 销量下滑 20%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，市场调研机构 Omdia 数据显示，2026 年第三季度，印度全国智能手机出货量同比下降 26%，创下过去 10 年同期最低水平。尽管苹果 iPhone 在印度的销量同比下滑 20%，但与竞争对手相比，其表现仍相对稳健。据悉，印度消费者的消费支出趋于保守，与新机涨价叠加在一起，该国智能手机总出货量降至 3580 万部。零售商也采取了更为谨慎的策略，在购物季到来前避免囤积过多库存。尽管销量下滑 20%，苹果仍以 390 万部的出货量位列印度智能手机市场第五，iPhone 16 和 iPhone 17 等标准版机型占大头。由于苹果今年没有推出 iPhone 18 标准版，因此不少消费者选择旧款产品。如今，手机厂商已不能再单纯依靠庞大的出货量推动印度业务增长，而是需要付出更多努力来说服消费者更换手机。在持续低迷的市场环境下，提供更有吸引力的以旧换新优惠、并突出高端调性的品牌，才更有可能站稳脚跟。

articles.title: 全新深蓝 S05 新增智能生态仪表屏：4.39 英寸 OLED，显示核心行车信息
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，深蓝汽车官方发布，全新深蓝 S05 新增智能生态仪表屏。此前，深蓝 S05 仅提供 AR-HUD 抬头显示，智能生态仪表屏采用 4.39 英寸 OLED 屏，信息一目了然。IT之家注意到，全新深蓝 S05 车型于今年 8 月上市，共推出 5 款车型，售价区间 11.99-15.19 万元，限时优惠价 11.59-14.49 万元。该车内饰采用悬浮星舰设计理念，提供星云紫、热浪橙、星岩灰三种配色。车内搭载 256 色悬浮式环抱氛围灯，并配备高级木纹理装饰面板。该车取消了传统液晶仪表盘，行车信息通过 HUD 抬头显示投射，车机系统升级为 DEEPAL OS 4.2，同时完善了手车互联、全座舱情景模式等功能，提供三辐多功能方向盘、手机无线充电、前排双杯架及电子怀挡。动力方面，全新深蓝 S05 延续在售车型，提供纯电和增程两种选择。纯电版搭载后置单电机，最大功率 272 马力，提供 56.12kWh 和 68.82kWh 两种电池容量，对应 CLTC 续航里程分别为 520km 和 620km。增程版由 1.5L 发动机（98 马力）搭配驱动电机（238 马力），配 28.39kWh 电池，纯电续航 215km，综合续航 1310km。

articles.title: 流媒体平台 Spotify 严厉打击家庭套餐共享，要求当面扫码验证
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，据科技媒体 Android Authority 今天报道，流媒体平台 Spotify 正严查家庭套餐共享行为，部分用户已经开始无法使用。IT之家从原报道获悉，部分家庭共享用户已经收到了重新验证住址提示。从官方口径来看，此次验证似乎需要当面完成：家庭成员需要扫描管理员手机上的二维码，确保双方住在同一个地方。并且，这个二维码每隔几秒钟就会刷新，因此不能截图分享。不过一些用户表示，他们通过屏幕共享，就轻松绕过了这种机制。Spotify 官方表示，用户收到通知后有 7 天时间完成重新验证。如果不理会通知或未完成验证，家庭订阅将自动降级至免费套餐，且 12 个月内禁止加入其他家庭或双人套餐，但个人套餐仍可订阅。早在 2018 年，Spotify 就试行过 GPS 验证，定期查验用户所在地。不过由于用户强烈反对，Spotify 最终放宽了这种限制。

articles.title: 商务部：今年 1-9 月，重点平台智能眼镜销售额增长 1.1 倍
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，国新办今日举行新闻发布会，介绍加快推进科技兴商有关情况。商务部部长助理袁晓明介绍，本次《关于加快推进科技兴商的意见》（IT之家注：以下简称《意见》）是立足新发展阶段，首次以“科技兴商”为主题，出台的一份综合性、系统性文件。核心是把科技创新作为贯穿商贸全链条的重要驱动力，推动科技与商贸深度融合。政策的主要特点，可以用三个字来概括：“新”“全”“实”。“新”，就是突出科技创新，适应消费新趋势新变化。随着人民生活水平提升，消费者更加注重产品的品质和消费体验。根据商务部商务大数据显示，今年 1-9 月，重点平台智能眼镜销售额增长 1.1 倍。人工智能、物联网、区块链等新技术，在消费领域广泛应用，科技创新日益成为推动消费扩容升级的重要举措。《意见》紧扣新一轮科技革命和产业变革，既立足当前扩大消费的现实需要，着力激活消费市场；又着眼长远发展，以科技创新改造提升传统商贸、培育壮大新兴业态，为商贸高质量发展注入持久动力。“全”，就是突出双向发力，覆盖商贸全链条全业态。纵向上，从供给端的产品研发、生产制造、服务提供，到流通端的批发、物流、电商，再到消费场景，将科技创新融入到商贸各环节。横向上，既用新技术改造提升零售、餐饮、家政等传统业态，让传统的消费焕发新活力；同时，也培育商业智能体、绿色循环消费等新业态新模式，让新型消费释放新动能，形成供需两端协同、传统消费与新型消费并举的完整政策体系。“实”，就是突出问题导向，确保政策可落地可检验。《意见》聚焦商贸领域突出问题精准施策。例如，针对商品供需适配问题，提出发展柔性制造、推广按需生产等模式，培育一批具有行业影响力的定制品牌。围绕丰富优质服务供给，提出推动家政、医疗、养老托育等民生服务数智化转型，拓展智慧教育、智慧文旅、智能体育等升级服务。针对电商品质问题，提出开展品质电商培育行动，加强重点产品电商平台联网核查。参考商务部等 9 部门关于加快推进科技兴商的意见

articles.title: 张雪官宣首款电摩明年上市，目标直指全球头部
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，据央视财经今日报道，张雪机车创始人张雪在“光华录”中聊到自家电摩规划，首款产品明年上市，目标直指全球头部，主打轻量化、强动力、高能效。张雪表示，两轮电动化有个很特别的红利 —— 新能源汽车提前铺好了遍布全国的充电桩，相当于汽车把路修好，电摩顺势登场。IT之家注意到，对于网友希望张雪机车推出踏板摩托的呼吁，张雪本人 4 月 7 日发视频表示，他们的踏板已经在做了。张雪在视频中说道：“最近很多车友都在催促我出踏板，说实话我们踏板在做了。但是我们做的还是运动加越野风格的踏板，会是一种有趣的好玩的，但售价还是相对会高一点，比传统的 125、150 肯定要高得多。”张雪今年 5 月就曾透露旗下首款电摩的开发进展，表示目前有一款电机已经接近开发成功，直径 200 毫米，重量 8 公斤，可输出 50 千瓦的功率。张雪机车创始人张雪于 7 月 19 日晒出一张 ZDYD 电机外特性曲线图，显示这款电机输出功率可达 50kW、扭矩可达 90N·m。

articles.content: Anthropic 代码量暴涨，GitHub 密钥扫描又慢又贵，两家被迫改造系统。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       Git 已经支撑软件开发二十多年，Anthropic 却决定把它换掉。为了让 Claude 持续生成的代码顺利进入开发流程，7 名工程师花了 5 个月，开发出版本控制系统 Scion，并将核心代码仓库迁移过去。今年 5 月，Anthropic 每天平均合并约 2500 项代码变更，到 9 月已超过 3 万项，仅 CI 系统每天就要执行约 2500 万次代码检出。写代码的速度上来了，准备仓库、同步对象和查询历史却越来越费机器。几乎同一时期，GitHub 用微调后的 ModernBERT 替换密钥扫描中的通用 LLM 判断。哥伦比亚大学与 Google DeepMind 等机构则通过 BTTF，把芯片仿真波形转换成 SQLite，让 Agent 使用 SQL 排查异常。Scion 默认在线，BTTF 将波形变成查询接口，GitHub 把高频判断交给分类器。围绕人类开发节奏设计的系统，开始承受 Agent 带来的另一种负载。01Git 的离线能力，为什么成了负担Git 的分布式设计让工程师克隆仓库后，即使断网也能提交、合并、查看历史。但 Anthropic 大量读取代码的任务是始终联网的 CI 作业和 Agent 沙箱，运行几分钟便销毁，可能只需要几个文件、一份 diff，或确认两个提交的祖先关系。为了这些操作准备本地仓库，重复成本越来越高。Anthropic 主分支历史接近 100 GB，压缩工作副本超过 25 GB。若每天 2500 万次检出分别获取完整副本，理论流量会超过 600 PB。公司虽用浅克隆、稀疏检出、快照和数百台 Git 镜像，但镜像仍要同步、快照会过期，历史查询还需补齐对象。仓库越活跃，维护成本越高。Scion 将客户端缩成轻量入口。提交创建、合并、变基与历史查询放到中心服务，本地仅监测文件变化、维护少量缓存，需要工作目录时按需展开。CI 若只想计算 diff，可以直接调用 API，无须完整检出。这牺牲了离线自治，却减少重复初始化。提交格式也变了。Git commit 指向描述仓库状态的目录树，Scion 的 changeset 则以预写日志条目记录相对首个父提交修改过的文件，通过内容寻址指针引用数据。创建 changeset 无须生成 Git packfile，也不用立即移动共享分支，只有 main 等引用更新时，系统才对 Spanner 中的单行记录执行 compare-and-swap。Agent 可以并发生成变更，竞争集中到分支引用移动时。但历史查询仍有难题：增量记录无法直接回答某行是谁改的、文件经历过什么。Scion 为 blame、路径历史与提交图跳表维护 derived data，按父提交关系预计算，或等查询发生后再生成。写入与历史分析可以独立扩展。雷峰网检出时，scn 客户端从目标目录树开始，只请求缺失的 tree 和 blob。请求依次经过节点上的 scion-daemon、区域 scion-cache，再由 scion-server 回源到 Spanner 或对象存储。对象写入后不可变，缓存能够跨任务复用，减少协商、压缩及反复传输。Anthropic 称缓存命中率超过 99%，并限制故障时的回源流量。迁移后，Scion 相较旧 Git 镜像体系的 CPU 和内存需求约缩小 200 倍，检出从分钟级降至秒级，CI 释放约 25% 的 CPU 容量。200 倍说的是基础设施资源占用，并非 Git 操作整体提速。Anthropic 还同步建设 Antique 代码评审、源码搜索、IAM 和批量合并工具，以适配新协议。在线服务的维护也成了新成本。02让数据库读波形，Agent 才能追查故障芯片验证面对的是另一种障碍。

articles.title: Muse Wonder 建模大翻车，亚历山大·王辩护遭马斯克无情补刀
articles.content: 官方承认 3D 短板，跨模型测试 Harness 不同。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       Meta 刚发布的 Muse Wonder，没想到因为一盏熔岩灯，在开发者社区引发了一场关于 AI 模型跑分的争论。10 月 12 日，Meta 推出 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full，主打 Coding Agent、工具调用和长任务执行能力。官方公布的成绩相当亮眼，Wonder Full 在 SWE-Marathon 上拿到 57.5 分，DeepSWE 1.1 达到 79.0 分，已经能够与同期的前沿模型展开竞争。然而，开发者社区 BridgeMind 随后安排了一项 3D 编程测试，要求 Muse Wonder 制作一盏具有透明玻璃外壳、动态熔岩和光照效果的熔岩灯。结果模型只生成了一个红色圆柱体。BridgeMind 随即质疑 Muse Wonder 存在严重的 Benchmaxxing，也就是针对 Benchmark 进行大量优化，成绩看着漂亮，碰上陌生任务却露了怯。连马斯克也忍不住下场，在相关帖子下意味深长地回了一句 Hmm。短短一个词，虽然没有明确表态，却让这场围绕 Meta 新模型的刷分争议又添了几分戏剧性。Meta 首席 AI 官 Alexandr Wang 很快回应，团队确实没有针对 3D 演示游戏进行显式训练，事后看来或许应该补充相关训练，但他仍然希望开发者实际体验 Muse Wonder 的 Coding 能力。雷峰网这场争论有一个重要前提：熔岩灯测试针对的是普通版 Muse Wonder，而 Meta 公布的部分突出成绩来自 Wonder Full，两者存在能力差异。同时，Meta 官方 Model Card 已经明确承认，视觉与空间推理，尤其是 3D 任务，属于 Muse Wonder 的已知短板。但高分模型在陌生任务中遭遇如此明显的失败，依然让人好奇：当前大模型的训练方法究竟在强化哪些能力，Agent Benchmark 又能在多大程度上反映模型的实际水平？01奖励机制，决定模型擅长解决什么问题Muse Wonder 的表现，与当前大模型越来越依赖 Post-training 提升任务能力的技术路线有关。在 Pre-training 阶段，模型通过大规模数据学习语言、代码、空间关系和其他通用知识。进入 Post-training 后，训练会进一步塑造模型的行为策略，尤其是通过强化学习，让它在特定任务环境中形成更稳定的执行能力。Coding Agent 很适合这类训练。例如，给模型一个存在 Bug 的代码仓库，要求它定位问题、修改文件并运行测试。整个过程可以通过编译结果、单元测试和功能检查获得相对明确的反馈。强化学习系统据此判断哪些操作有效，持续强化能够提高任务成功率的行为。训练规模扩大后，模型逐渐学会一套复杂的软件工程策略，包括如何缩小搜索范围、选择工具、处理报错，以及在多轮修改中维护任务状态。Meta 在官方技术文章中提到，Muse Wonder 接受了多样化长任务训练，并引入 Active Focus，使模型能够在遭遇阻碍后尝试其他方案、恢复执行并继续推进任务。但这类训练依赖一个关键条件：环境必须能够向模型提供有用的反馈。熔岩灯恰好打破了传统 Coding Agent 熟悉的反馈方式。雷峰网从程序实现来看，熔岩灯涉及三维几何、透明材质、光照计算和动态形变。如果使用 Three.js，模型需要构造玻璃灯罩，为内部熔岩生成不规则的几何形态，再通过时间变量或噪声函数驱动形状变化。这些代码即使能够正常执行，画面仍然可能完全错误。例如，透明材质的参数配置不当，玻璃就可能变成不透明的实体，熔岩形状缺少连续变化机制，内部效果就可能退化为静态色块。编译器和单元测试很难直接判断这些视觉问题。这意味着，Agent 还需要具备一套

articles.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22373v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. articles.title: Rethinking User Encoders: Routing Diffusion States for Scenario-Adaptive User Representation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22400v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM)-based user encoders serialize heterogeneous behavioral logs and compress them into static representations through autoregressive (AR) prediction. However, their unidirectional constraint limits bidirectional information flow, hindering cross-modal interactions and the joint preservation of multi-source signals. Consequently, the learned static representations struggle to accommodate the distinct evidence requirements of diverse downstream scenarios. We address these limitations by unlocking the iterative denoising process of diffusion language models (dLLMs) as a multi-granularity reconstruction space. Based on this insight, we propose FINDERS (FactorIzatioN of Diffusion statEs for Routing across Scenarios), a router-equipped dLLM framework comprising four operations: denoise, factorize, route, and compress. articles.title: From Events to Reasoning: Hierarchical Rule Composition over Explicit States
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22403v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What a reasoning system emits is a conclusion; what it owes is a justification. Producing one requires every operation to be admissible on the facts actually available, the dependencies of intermediate results to survive to the end of the path, and the path to be revised when a premise changes. We present the Event Reasoning System (ERS), in which the reasoning state is an explicit event graph. Semantic features nominate candidate objects and rule bindings, and declared rule and task conditions decide which may execute, so candidates that violate the represented period, unit, or evidence constraints cannot enter an accepted reasoning path. Low-level rules provide reusable local transformations, and recursively composable high-level control rules organize subgoals and legal paths under the current goal, information gaps, and budget; a finite library is thereby rebound into paths never stored as complete solutions. articles.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. articles.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22420v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent-based models are well-suited for modelling agro-ecological systems for decision-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours. In such a context, sensitivity analysis stumbles upon a structural feature of many complex systems: the parameters are not a flat vector but a decision tree in which many parameters appear only when a higher-level choice activates them. Classical global sensitivity analysis presupposes independent inputs over a fixed Cartesian product and is ill-posed on such a branched space and biased by construction. We instead treat the structure of the decisions as a first-class modelling object. Using advanced surrogate modelling techniques, we encode the crop-management itinerary of the high-resolution agro-ecological modelling platform MAELIA as a hierarchical design space featuring both categorical and numerical variables. articles.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22426v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. articles.title: From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22441v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. articles.title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22446v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. Efficient grid-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator (FNO) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes. We introduce L-SplineFNO, a memory-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution. articles.title: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22460v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue. We argue this is a mistake. Whatever their moral status, models exhibit welfare-like states that causally influence their behaviour. Following recent work, we adopt the term 'functional welfare' for these states. We make three claims. First, functional welfare already arises naturally and will become more robust as models acquire more coherent goals and personas. Second, functional welfare should be treated as a safety variable: it should inform evaluation design, be tracked in monitoring, and be a direct target of post-training. Third, against existing scepticism about measuring AI welfare, we argue that good empirical work on functional welfare is possible. articles.title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. articles.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22466v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. articles.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22469v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. articles.title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) that leverage test-time computation achieve strong performance on mathematical and scientific benchmarks and are increasingly deployed in real-world applications. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics---ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving long-standing open conjectures---have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve. Yet these successes primarily concern predefined, human-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions. To push beyond static challenges, we explore the Busy Beaver (BB) domain, an uncomputable frontier that is fundamentally open-ended. Because no algorithm can compute the Busy Beaver number $\mathrm{BB}(n)$ for every $n$, this domain provides a natural setting for sustained exploration through mathematical conjecture and proof. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22668v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-term memory enables LLM agents to reuse past experiences, yet retrieving relevant memories does not necessarily provide sufficient evidence for answering a query. Essential information may remain fragmented across memory records, obscured by abstraction, or disconnected from the relations required for reasoning. We identify this relevance-sufficiency gap and propose QEMem, a framework that reformulates memory utilization as the construction of query-specific evidence sets, shifting the focus from individual retrieval relevance to collective evidential support. QEMem integrates three complementary mechanisms: query-guided discovery retrieves evidence across multiple memory granularities; source-grounded reification organizes it into structured ViewCards with explicit evidential roles and source references; and sufficiency-guided refinement selectively recovers missing information. Abstract: Modern mobile GUI agents can perceive visible screens and execute local actions, but they still lack persistent app-specific navigation knowledge: where functions live, which pages contain them, and which screens are equivalent across repeated visits. We introduce TAG-Nav, a Task-Agnostic Graph Navigation framework that wraps existing GUI-agent backbones with reusable destination memory. Offline exploration is distilled into compact records of app functions, target pages, and waypoint routes before any evaluated instruction is seen. When a future task's destination is covered, TAG-Nav retrieves the destination and provides route guidance without task-specific demonstrations. arXiv:2610.22682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) can integrate understanding and generation within a single backbone. However, it is commonly known that these two capabilities can cause conflicting representations, leading to a central question: how representation and computation should be shared across functionalities? Existing UMMs often rely on a largely fixed structure, where different inputs and functionalities follow the same depth and parameter-sharing pattern. We argue that this assumption is too restrictive: more effective unification requires sharing the computation that supports cross-functional communication while specializing the capacity that becomes task- or input-specific. We introduce FlexUMM, a flexible UMM framework that dynamically decides when to preserve shared computation, when to route specialized capacity, and when to stop further processing. articles.content:

Abstract: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. We reopen this design space by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates. Missing positions follow absorbing dynamics, while context undergoes low-rate random substitution, exposing the model to observed but uncertain tokens during training. At inference, a heuristic sampler re-injects noise into suspicious context under an annealed intensity and freezes context updates late in the trajectory. Abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable-specific dynamics and cross-variable interactions. An innovative reservoir design is proposed in which inter-cluster connections are enabled by empirically observed correlations among variables, providing a data-driven coupling mechanism. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22433v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. The root bound certifies a completed schedule's suboptimality gap without a solver. On industry-motivated 10-module prefabricated-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%. Abstract: Distributed Transformer inference across co-located edge devices is fundamentally communication-bound, as exchanging activations between sequence-parallel partitions dominates inference latency under commodity edge bandwidths. Abstract: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine-tunes without alignment content. Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22467v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities. One prominent approach is self-distillation, where a model is trained to match the token-level predictions it would have produced when given access to additional context, such as a cue, feedback, or instruction. However, the safety properties of this training procedure are poorly understood. In this paper, we present a surprising safety failure of recursive self-distillation, where each self-distilled model becomes the teacher for the next round of training. We observe that when a safe model is recursively self-distilled on its own (safe) generations while receiving an additional non-harmful cue, it becomes increasingly misaligned across a diverse set of harmful queries; we call this Progressive Misalignment. articles.title: Generative Value Classifier
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22497v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Q-learning is premised on learning a function to predict the value of a state-action pair, with the goal of using such a function to guide policy improvement. Most approaches learn this function from scratch using scalar or distributional return targets. This discriminative approach leaves another source of supervision for learning representations unused: the actions themselves. Rather than directly predict the return of a state-action pair, we ask the reverse question: how likely is the action under each possible return? This perspective provides a critic whose generative component is a return-conditioned policy, which can share the actor's architecture. Training this policy supervises the critic with every action rather than with returns alone, and a squared-error loss anchors the critic's Q-value to the bootstrapped target. Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22428v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed. We ask what that table actually buys. We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it. The learned table buys 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, but on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA the frozen-table model is better or tied; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions on short-answer question answering in four MoE families. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly. In Qwen3-30B-A3B this loss is made at the two chat-template tokens before the answer, and in DeepSeek-V2-Lite at the first 8-32 prompt tokens, where its instruction sits; by answer likelihood these positions account for about half and a fifth of the damage. Reduction changes the first token's attention mass, norm and largest activation by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most about a quarter of the loss, well below keeping the sensitive positions full. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22468v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Action nominal constructions (ANCs) express events in nominal form, with their argument marking following patterns found in clauses or ordinary noun phrases. In this paper, we investigate how different grammatical configurations affect language models' learning of ANCs and related constructions, and how these learning preferences compare with typological distributions in natural languages. We use a grammar-engineered method for synthetic corpus construction that combines shared semantic input from natural corpora with computational grammars. We construct 96 target languages varying in clause word order, noun-phrase word order, alignment, complement system, and ANC strategy. For each language, we train GPT-2-small models from scratch and evaluate them using targeted minimal pairs covering 34 grammatical phenomena. The results show typological parallels in basic clause configurations but divergences in complement systems and ANC strategies

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. In this paper, we present REALCLI, a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks. To comprehensively measure collaboration, REALCLI builds a five-dimensional framework, operationalized into 22 sub-dimensions and 51 interaction scenario templates. REALCLI provides two modes for paired comparison: REALCLI-EXEC supplies complete specifications upfront, whereas REALCLI-COLLAB introduces a scripted user that delivers progressive information, corrections, constraint revisions, and authorization decisions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating language models and agents requires combining benchmark accuracy, judge-based assessment, runtime performance, tool-use behavior, and retrieval quality. Differences in interfaces, metric semantics, and trace formats complicate these comparisons and can hide failures in agentic workflows. We present AuditKIT, a source-available evaluation library that records these measurements in one result representation, with direction-aware metric contracts, configuration fingerprints, and extensible metrics and backends. For agents, it provides turn-aware tool-call matching, separates parallel from sequential execution, and distinguishes verified task outcomes from trajectory-level diagnostics. Missing or unobservable evidence is marked unscored rather than counted as failure. articles.title: alkhder at ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks: Constrained Selection and Rotation-Averaged Logit Scoring for Multimodal Hallucination Detection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22515v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We describe our submission to Subtask~1b of ImageEval 2026. The task consists of selecting the single visually valid statement from three candidates paired with an image, and is in both English and Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). Our system uses a pre-trained 7B vision--language model in a zero-shot setting, without task-specific training or fine-tuning. We formulate the task as a constrained selection problem and choose the answer using next-token log-probabilities. To reduce answer-position bias, we apply a Latin-square rotation to the candidate statements. Our system achieves CI scores of 0.0510 on the English test set and 0.0960 on the MSA test set, reducing CI relative to the official 3B baselines reported on devtest by 83.7\% and 80.4\%, respectively.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: User simulators enable interactive training and evaluation of AI assistants at scale. Yet current simulators struggle to reproduce the diverse behaviors of real users, leading to assistants that generalize poorly to underrepresented users. We identify user representations as an underexplored bottleneck in user simulation. User representations are natural-language descriptions that condition simulators to reproduce a particular user's behavior. A representation's quality becomes apparent in hindsight, through the behavior it induces in a simulator. To evaluate and optimize user representations, we formulate a conversation reconstruction task: given an original conversation, we generate a representation, condition a simulator on it, simulate a conversation, and then measure fidelity by comparing user behavior in the original and simulated conversations. articles.title: alkhder at AlexandriaX-2026: Context-Aware English-to-Dialectal Arabic Dialogue Translation with QLoRA-Fine-Tuned NileChat-3B
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22525v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper describes team Alkhder's submission to Subtask 1 of the AlexandriaX-2026 shared task, which asks systems to translate English dialogue turns into thirteen Arabic dialects. We fine-tune NileChat-3B-Base with QLoRA on the Alexandria parallel dialogue corpus, training one set of adapter weights for all dialects. Each turn is translated conditioned on the target country and dialect, the domain, the participant roles, the speaker-addressee gender direction, and the preceding dialogue context. At inference, conversations are translated autoregressively and the model is fed its own previous outputs back as context without using any gold target-side test information. Under the constrained track, using only Alexandria data, it trains in about one hour and translates the private test set in under two hours. The system reaches a country-macro-averaged spBLEU of 20.36 and chrF++ of 36.64 on both tracks.

Abstract: Decision models, non-generative scorers that report a probability over caller-supplied options and emit no text, are increasingly deployed as routers, classifiers and guardrails. articles.title: Pearl-Chat: Engineering a native Luganda language model from first principles in JAX and Flax NNX
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive foundation language models predominantly target high-resource Indo-European languages, imposing computational and morphological penalties on under-represented African languages. Generic multilingual tokenizers routinely exceed fertility rates of 3.2 tokens per word on agglutinative Bantu languages, degrading context efficiency and inflating latency. We present Pearl-Chat, an 8,473,122-parameter ($\sim$8.5M) causal decoder-only transformer engineered for Luganda (Oluganda, ISO 639-2: lg), a low-resource Niger-Congo Bantu language spoken by over 10 million people in East Africa. Built from first mathematical principles in JAX and Flax NNX, Pearl-Chat uses explicit functional state decomposition (nnx.split and nnx.merge), deterministic resumable data streaming via Google Grain, and SPMD tensor parallelism using jax.sharding.Mesh. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in English Relation Extraction (RE) tasks, a significant gap remains in assessing their RE performance in low-resource languages, due to a lack of standardized benchmarks. Creating native, language-specific annotated RE benchmarks is expensive and requires human expertise, while relying on translation yields suboptimal, inaccurate datasets that introduce English-centric biases. To tackle this, we propose a scalable, language-agnostic methodology to create RE data by denoising naturally occurring yet noisy alignments of knowledge bases and corresponding texts. We define a proper alignment via a Natural Language Inference (NLI) task, where a relation triplet is entailed by an input text. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22545v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stereotypes are subjective constructs that are mediated by the cultural context in which they are viewed. Successfully modeling them thus also requires cultural competence. When using large language models (LLMs) for stereotype-related tasks, such as their detection, it is therefore crucial that models can access relevant cultural knowledge and adjust responses accordingly. Since LLMs have shown disparities in what cultural knowledge is available to them, their capacity regarding stereotypes may also be disparate across languages and cultural contexts (e.g., for non-English languages or for non-US contexts). In this paper, we systematically investigate the effectiveness of LLMs for culture-specific stereotype detection across three factors: (1) the prompting language, (2) the instruction tuning language, and (3) the fine-tuning dataset size. Abstract: Successful completion of perspectivist natural language processing (NLP) annotation tasks requires algorithms to be aligned across diverse perspectives in order to predict how different humans will rate text. This work studies how the performance of such algorithms varies for annotators who behave differently than others, either by providing annotations that diverge from others' responses or by providing fewer annotations altogether. To aid with characterizing model performance, we curate the largest collection to date of perspectivist NLP datasets with ordinal annotations. After evaluating multiple classes of perspectivist algorithms across each of the datasets, we model the relationship between individual annotator idiosyncrasy and algorithm performance. Abstract: We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups. Our results show that ADV-RoBERTa improves classification performance and alignment between explanations and human rationales while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Strong multi-hop retrieval should be practical to deploy without expensive corpus preparation or complex database infrastructure. We present SAG2, an embedding-free retrieval architecture built around a single SQLite database, BM25, and contextual evidence decisions from JEV. SAG2 follows the query-time association principle of SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), while replacing its event-entity and dense indexes with a lexical index over original passages. Selected passages supply terms for further retrieval, and newly retrieved evidence guides subsequent decisions. This moves semantic evidence selection to query time, eliminating offline embedding computation, LLM-based event-entity extraction, and dedicated database servers. articles.title: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22594v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical multi-agent systems, in which LLM agents discuss a case, are increasingly studied for clinical decision support. Prompt injection, text that an attacker adds to a model's input, can manipulate LLMs into wrong decisions. How it affects these systems, and how to protect them, remains unclear. Across two systems, two model families and three benchmarks, a single injected passage succeeds in up to 61% of cases, and collaboration does not consistently protect against it. Existing defenses help only partly: they miss injections that look like ordinary clinical text. Yet when asked to check the injected text against the patient's findings, a model that followed the injection usually rejects it. We therefore propose a training-free defense that verifies the clinical judgments behind the system's decision. Abstract: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models must efficiently find identifiers across diverse contexts while maintaining a low false-positive rate (FPR) on high-volume traffic. Recent detectors increasingly rely on complex architectures that raise deployment cost, yet many are fine-tuned on only a few synthetic datasets that limit their coverage. Combining public datasets is challenging because their taxonomies differ, and even after categories are mapped to a common schema, labels can disagree on what counts as a detection, producing inconsistent training and evaluation signals. To address these problems, we present a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based detector trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a detailed definition of broad contextual detection for 12 structured PII categories. Abstract: Uncertainty can measure hallucination risk in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), but only when retrieved evidence constrains the answer. Varying retrieval depth shows why the score changes meaning: detection can weaken with only the top-ranked passage, then recover after adding a second passage. Abstract: Large language models rely on spurious features in clinical classification: swapping a single gender token in clinical notes alters gender-irrelevant diagnoses in up to 53.5% of cases. Abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). To facilitate research on Event-STVG, we construct a large-scale benchmark comprising 4,016 annotated event occurrences across soccer and seven additional domains. Abstract: Human communication is inherently multimodal, conveying intent not only through linguistic and vocal cues but also through visual signals. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable 3D person detection is important for rescue robotics to give first responders situational awareness. Yet most multimodal 3D detection research targets automotive scenarios in which pedestrians mostly appear in a narrow range of upright, near-road poses. It is therefore unclear how much of the reported performance transfers to rescue settings, as a person may be lying, partially occluded, or in unstructured indoor and outdoor environments. To investigate this gap, we introduce TriSAR-3D, a multimodal person detection dataset recorded with a high-resolution 128-channel LiDAR, an RGB camera, and a thermal camera. It captures varied poses in indoor as well as outdoor locations at different times of day to study their influence on 3D object detector performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22514v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Internet-scale photo collections of real-world landmarks have driven progress in 3D computer vision yet remain highly challenging for modern 3D foundation models (3DFMs) that estimate scene structure in a single feed-forward pass. In this work, we introduce ArchWorld, a benchmark of 3D architectural landmarks with high geographic coverage and rich metadata. We use this benchmark to conduct a thorough error analysis of current 3DFMs to understand where they fall short and how they can be improved. We examine socially relevant disparities in model error and find that model performance varies by geographic region; however, unlike typical fairness regimes, the trends only partially match training data representation. Abstract: Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a powerful tool. Cryo-EM produces noisy two-dimensional particle images in which molecular structure, particle pose, and imaging conditions are jointly encoded. Recovering biological information from these observations spans inverse problems including pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction. These tasks are usually addressed independently despite shared protein structure and image formation, motivating a common representation across inverse problems. articles.title: FlashControl: One-Step Controllable Generator via Distillation-Friendly Single-Stream Teachers
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22537v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion models have become a leading approach in visual generative modeling, particularly effective in text-to-image and controllable generation. Their main drawback is slow inference as it requires many sampling steps. While recent distillation methods enable one-step text-to-image generation, extending these techniques to controllable generation is still challenging. Existing controllable models, such as ControlNet, rely on dual-branch design that make distillation difficult. In this work, we adopt a simpler strategy. Instead of adding extra conditional branches, we finetune a selected subset of layers in the original text-to-image diffusion model to directly enable controllable generation. This results in DeltaControl, a single-flow, multi-step diffusion model capable of supporting spatial-condition generation while matching the performance of dual-branch approaches. articles.title: CFC26: Building Evaluations for Deployment in Sonar-Based Fish Counting
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate counts of fish populations are essential for monitoring ecosystems and making decisions for conservation, harvest limits, and river management. In many field deployments, these counts are obtained from sonar videos that experts must inspect manually, making large-scale monitoring slow, expensive, and difficult. Automated counting systems have been proposed as a scalable alternative, but so far this promise has been difficult to realize in deployment. Developing evaluations that better reflect real-world deployment conditions will help close this gap and drive improvements in counting performance in practice. To achieve this, we propose Caltech Fish Counting 2026 (CFC26), a new dataset with improved evaluation protocols that simulate deployment to seen and novel rivers, testing in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22566v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manual annotation of synchronized video and EEG recordings is a bottleneck in preclinical seizure research. We present an empirical study of seizure detection and behavioral severity grading using 24,131 paired clips from 601 sessions across 20 rats in a soman-induced epilepsy model. Ten video architectures and seven single-channel EEG models are evaluated independently on binary detection and three- and five-class severity tasks. In the session-exclusive reference comparison, R(2+1)D-18 and GRU achieve detection macro-F1 scores of 0.968 and 0.974, respectively; for five-class grading, the corresponding scores are 0.657 and 0.560. Subject-exclusive evaluation reduces five-class macro-F1 to 0.475 for video and 0.404 for EEG, highlighting the difficulty of grading unseen animals. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22602v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval is a fundamental task in multimodal systems: given an image or text query, the goal is to find the most relevant images or texts in a collection, often using a shared embedding space. Reliable retrieval requires these embeddings to capture not only which concepts are present, but also how they are composed. One key compositional challenge is attribute--object binding: encoding which attributes belong to which objects. Existing benchmarks provide a limited view of this capability, typically covering a subset of modality pairings, simple two-object swaps, or small attribute sets. Consequently, it remains unclear how robustly current models preserve attribute--object bindings across different modality pairings and more complex settings. arXiv:2610.22606v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: FOR-species20K is the largest public LiDAR benchmark for tree-species classification, pooling 25 independently collected terrestrial, mobile, and airborne laser-scanning datasets across 33 species. We introduce a multi-resolution, multi-view ConvNeXtV2 model that improves official hidden-test accuracy from 79.5% to 85.0%, ranking first at the time of submission. We then examine what this score measures. Because the hidden test is species-balanced, its overall accuracy is more comparable to a macro metric than to accuracy under the public set's long-tailed distribution. Moreover, the official random split places every source dataset in both training and evaluation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22608v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in video generation let users create high-quality videos from natural language descriptions, yet obtaining results that match user intent remains time-consuming: individual generations are computationally expensive, and underspecified prompts force repeated cycles of generation, inspection, and revision. Existing video prompt optimization methods improve generation through automatic rewriting, but cannot supply the ideas and preferences that were not in the initial description. We propose ProactGen, a video generation framework that learns proactive clarification, eliciting user intent through questions grounded in generated video drafts. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22610v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are usually chosen from leaderboards, which give one ranking for every application. On questions about objects that a scene suggests but does not contain, however, the model with the lowest error on the POPE hallucination benchmark is not the one with the lowest error on such questions. For yes/no questions about object presence, we show that the best model for a target domain can be predicted without running any candidate on that domain, given 650 to 1,200 labeled target items that calibrate a detector. We measure each model's reliance on a cue, a feature such as scene context or text in the image, by editing 100 labeled source images so that the cue suggests the wrong answer, and comparing with a matched control edit. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22676v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthetic facial imagery has made the distinction between authentic and generated content increasingly important for digital forensics and online trust. This study examines an explainable deep-learning workflow for image-level deepfake detection using two contrasting classification strategies: a compact convolutional model trained from scratch and an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 model adapted through two-stage transfer learning. Experiments were conducted with the balanced 140k Real and Fake Faces dataset, comprising 140,000 facial images. Under the recorded validation protocol, the augmented from-scratch model reached 84.15% accuracy (loss 0.3625), compared with 95.90% accuracy (loss 0.1074) for the fine-tuned pretrained model. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Answering complex spatial reasoning questions from egocentric video requires determining what evidence is needed, acquiring targeted observations, and combining them through multiple reasoning steps. Existing vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to perform this process reliably. Agentic systems address this challenge by querying external vision and geometry tools, but training their reasoning leaves these tools unchanged, so inaccurate observations can still lead to incorrect answers. We introduce EgoP$^{2}$C, a framework that internalizes a plan-perceive-compose process within a single VLM. To this end, we first train specialized Planner and Perception teachers using separate adapters (Dual-LoRA), then fine-tune the corresponding experts in a mixture-of-experts (MoE) student under their supervision. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22700v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) organize observations primarily in time, but embodied spatial reasoning requires organizing them in space. Consequently, their visual representations can remain locally consistent across nearby frames while lacking a persistent spatial context that is stable across viewpoints and time. We exploit depth and camera pose, which are naturally available to embodied agents, to explicitly establish this spatial correspondence. We introduce Cambrian-BEV, which extends Cambrian-S with a parameter-free geometric tokenization scheme that back-projects visual patch features from each frame into a shared bird's-eye-view (BEV) coordinate frame and averages features that fall within the same spatial cell. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22720v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-fidelity 3D generative modeling underpins game asset creation, medical imaging, and VR/AR environmental design, where geometric structure directly influences perception and decision-making. Diffusion models represent a powerful paradigm for point cloud generation. However, existing approaches rely heavily on local voxel or patch features and often miss global structural organization, and much less work has studied how global conditioning can be used to improve generation quality. In this paper, we introduce HilbertGen-3D, a novel topology-aware conditional diffusion framework based on Hilbert-Multifractal Conditioning (HMC). articles.title: Improving OCR Accuracy Through Multi-Classifier Verification of Visually Similar Characters
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22726v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distinguishing visually similar characters is a persistent challenge for optical character recognition (OCR) systems, causing errors in critical applications of text digitization. While preprocessing techniques improve image quality and word-level post-processing corrects spelling errors, neither addresses character-level visual ambiguity, an intrinsic property of certain character pairs that limits even state-of-the-art OCR models. We present the Character Verification Model (CVM), a character-level post-processing framework that verifies and corrects ambiguous characters in OCR outputs using specialized binary classifiers trained on visually confusable pairs such as 'O'/'0', 'Z'/'2', and 'S'/'5'. CVM operates independently of dictionary validation, making it suitable for non-lexical data including serial numbers, alphanumeric codes, and license plates. Abstract: Creative intent in video editing can be expressed through text instructions (e.g., "remove the people"), image references (e.g., subject appearance), video references (e.g., camera movement), or a combination of the above. Abstract: Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving. Generative world models can expand scenarios and predict future observations, yet may introduce content unsupported by measurements. We propose DriveWorld3D, a framework combining temporal video learning, measurement constraints from multiple sensors, and offline generative simulation. Its online component maintains a unified world state comprising road surfaces, volumetric occupancy, dynamic entities, and road relations, while separately representing physical occupancy, observability, and evidence provenance. articles.title: Mothership: A Two Tier Autonomous Refuse Collection System for Pedestrian Campuses
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Refuse collection in pedestrian campuses, parks and mixed-use districts remains manual because compaction trucks cannot reach bins located on walkways, courtyards and building service doors. This paper presents Mothership, a two-tier autonomous refuse collection system in which an electric compaction truck (the mothership) carries two low-speed sidewalk robots (RoboCarts) that fetch standard two-wheel bins, deliver them to the truck, return the empty bins to their original positions and re-dock on the truck for charging. The architecture separates responsibilities by scale: the truck performs road driving, compaction, lifting and energy supply, while the carts perform only sidewalk transport and bin grasping. This split removes the lift-and-tip mechanism from the sidewalk vehicle, keeping it light and low, and relaxes cart-to-truck docking tolerance to the +/-100 mm capture window of a standard automated lifter. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22471v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Abstract: Robot learning has advanced by scaling demonstration datasets and model capacity; however, deploying a new robot embodiment or task typically necessitates a dedicated teleoperation corpus. The resulting policies remain bounded by their imitation distributions, limiting generalization and continual self-improvement. We introduce RAX (Robot Agent eXploration), an open-source framework for robot agents centered on scaling exploration: enabling agents to improve by acquiring online experience and synthesizing executable programs. In RAX, a general-purpose coding agent generates robot control code, operating without action demonstration data, hand-engineered action primitives, or value-function guidance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22552v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Echolocating bats navigate dense forests using sonar alone, and in-air 3D imaging sonars now capture the entire frontal hemisphere with every pulse. Sonar SLAM, however, has so far been planar: current systems estimate a 2D trajectory and discard the elevation information in the sonar images, an assumption that does not hold on rough and sloped terrain such as a forest floor. In this paper, we introduce RTISSLAM-3D, a novel 6-DoF SLAM system for a wheeled robot that carries an in-air 3D imaging sonar, an IMU and wheel encoders. A CFAR detector on the sphere reduces every sonar image to a sparse set of 3D detections, which we use for a 3D acoustic odometry that models the shape of the sonar beam, for place recognition with polar submap descriptors, and for the verification of loop closures by 3D registration, all combined in a 6-DoF pose graph with attitude factors. articles.content:

Abstract: Long-horizon, multi-stage Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often require visual information that is no longer present in the current observation. Retaining the complete observation history is computationally expensive and highly redundant, motivating selective visual memory. Under receding-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single-task autoregressive decoder-only and Flow-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ policies over MIKASA-Robo-VLA tasks. Abstract: Flow-based policies such as $\pi_0$ are trained on a fixed set of embodiments, and transferring them to new ones is an open problem. Abstract: Quadruped parkour policies handle canonical obstacles well, but their training curricula often miss the irregular, compound geometry of industrial and disaster-response sites, where agile locomotion matters most. Such environments pose a hard generalization problem: even training directly on reconstructed geometry from the target site does not reliably yield policies that traverse it. Hand-designed curricula span only a few terrain families, and recent LLM-generated curricula offer little control over which policy weaknesses they target. We propose FCTS, a failure-conditioned terrain curriculum framework that uses localized traversal failures to automatically generate the terrains a policy should train on next. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22670v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-robot authoring can reduce completion time by distributing drawing work, but the resulting speedup depends on task structure and the allocation-routing pipeline. We investigate these relationships by representing drawings as geometric stroke graphs and comparing component-level (single-token) allocation with shared-token (decomposed) allocation, which permits multiple robots to work within a connected component. A simulation study of 385 drawings and teams of one to eight robots shows diminishing speedup gains under single-token allocation and larger mean speedups under the shared-token pipeline, each normalized by its own single-robot completion time. Shared-token execution also exhibits lower idle-time shares at larger team sizes, although it does not reduce completion time for every drawing. articles.title: Spatial Memory by Agents, for Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22736v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial memory enables robots to reuse past observations for localization, navigation, and question answering. Designing such memory involves jointly deciding what to retain and how to retrieve it for diverse semantic, metric, and temporal needs. We investigate whether coding agents can automate this design process through iterative implementation and evaluation. Under a fixed development budget, a Designer Agent writes and revises code for memory construction and retrieval using feedback from a fixed Query Agent. The resulting implementations are frozen before building memories from held-out observation histories, without access to downstream questions, and evaluated across five complementary task tracks using the same Query Agent. articles.title: Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22762v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rigid-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments. This coupling makes planning chal- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry. We propose Shape- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel-time, or cost- to-go, representation for rigid-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses. Abstract: Precise pedicel-targeted grasping in strawberry harvesting remains a critical bottleneck due to the pedicel's small diameter (1.3-3 mm), color similarity with surrounding foliage, and precise force control required for clean abscission zone detachment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22812v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires not only understanding instructions but also determining whether and how a robot can physically execute them. However, existing VLN benchmarks typically assume executable instructions and focus on long-horizon tasks. This leaves body-dependent local execution, including passability and collision-free execution, largely unexamined. Evaluating these factors within long-horizon tasks would entangle local physical execution with task planning and long-term spatial memory, making navigation failures difficult to attribute. We therefore focus on grounding local navigation commands in executable motion under environmental and robot body constraints. articles.title: Simultaneous Force and Motion Control in Generalised Coordinates
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22813v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot manipulators often come into contact with rigid objects when performing work. This imposes physical constraints on their motion. Simultaneous force & motion control was developed to regulate contact forces commensurate with these constraints, whilst projecting motion control in to the orthogonal, unconstrained directions. This is typically formulated in the task coordinates, i.e. operational space, then mapped to joint torques to command the robot. However, most constraints on the robot control, such as joint limits, collision avoidance, singularity avoidance, etc. are naturally expressed in generalised coordinates (joint space). Thus, formulating the control problem in task space makes it difficult to guarantee control feasibility. articles.title: DefFlow: Goal-Conditioned Deformable Object Manipulation using 3D Point Flows
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating deformable objects toward desired 3D configurations is a fundamental capability for robots operating in unstructured physical environments. However, as the range of possible initial and target configurations grows, goal-conditioned deformable manipulation requires a robot to infer increasingly diverse manipulation behaviors in addition to precise continuous actions. We introduce DefFlow, a framework for goal-conditioned manipulation of deformable objects toward a broad range of 3D configurations. DefFlow learns from demonstrations by jointly predicting the goal-conditioned 3D point flow of the robot and deformable object. We show that this formulation better captures both the manipulation decisions, such as when and where to grasp, release, or re-grasp, and the precise continuous motions required for goal reaching, rather than predicting only the robot flow. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22852v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generalist robot policies offer strong behavioral priors, but achieving deployment-level reliability and throughput remains difficult. Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve these policies, yet its effectiveness is constrained by the cost of online interaction. We introduce AnchorQ, which enables coarse-to-fine policy improvement through a structured, refinable latent action representation. articles.title: Structured Perception Representations for Off-road Dynamics Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomously navigating off-road terrain at high speed demands accurate control, which often relies on dynamics models that capture complex interactions between the robot and terrain. In off-road regimes, terrain interaction is a major component of the vehicle's dynamics. Prior work attempts to capture this effect by training learned models of the vehicle's dynamics, conditioned on its perception of the local environment. However, said conditioning is often overly simplistic, ignoring the spatial structure of the dynamics problem. Our approach, SpatialBEV, exploits this spatial structure. At each step, we query the bird's-eye-view (BEV) features around the predicted state, conditioning the next prediction on current geometric and semantic cues. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A robot swarm covers a building faster with more robots, but the map is only as complete as the space the robots have physically visited. We target the amount of an unknown building a decentralized swarm knows at each instant, ahead of physical coverage. SenseSwarm serves a lightweight learned map predictor on the swarm's shared occupancy map and folds the predicted structure back into a stigmergic guidance field. articles.title: Ego2Contact: Predicting Touch from Egocentric Human Video for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22932v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Contact locations and interaction forces are critical for contact-rich robot manipulation but are often ambiguous from vision alone. Measuring them on robots requires specialized tactile hardware and platform-specific data collection, which keeps robot tactile data scarce. Human egocentric video is far easier to scale but lacks touch. Recent predictors trained on egocentric recordings paired with tactile-glove measurements can predict this missing signal from video alone. These predictors, however, remain confined to human hands, which differ from robot hands in appearance and tactile layout. We present Ego2Contact, which learns a visual-tactile prior from human interactions and transfers it to robot hands. articles.title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
articles.content: Generated videos often lose geometric consistency under camera motion: structures warp under viewpoint change, parallax becomes inconsistent, and smooth camera movement may collapse into shot-like transitions. We argue that this failure is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. To address this, we propose Video Geometry Corrector (VGC), a post-hoc video-to-video model trained on synthetic paired supervision. Starting from real videos with diverse camera motion and pose annotations, we construct VG-Pairs with a synthetic paired-supervision data generation pipeline. Each video clip is treated as a geometry-consistent target and paired with a distorted counterpart synthesized by a pretrained image-to-video inpainting model using trajectory-adaptive keyframes. VGC learns to map the distorted input to the geometry-consistent target without modifying the source generator, and uses optical flow as an auxiliary cue to help disentangle camera motion from object motion. Experiments on pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks show that VGC improves geometric consistency across multiple source generators, and scaling to a larger backbone further extends the framework toward more general video refinement.

articles.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.

articles.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
articles.content: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich assembly, where the robot must find a millimeter-scale opening, mesh gear teeth, or catch a thread through light contact? We study this question by training blind assembly policies that observe only a short history of joint positions, velocities, and their own actions, without visual, force, torque, or tactile sensing. The poses of both the fixture and the part are unknown to the policy, and the grasp is randomized substantially. The policy must therefore assemble the parts through contact, sensed exclusively through its own proprioception. Trained with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts, such policies learn peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading. The peg insertion policy transfers zero-shot to the real world and inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 73% of trials. Controlled comparisons with matched visual policies in simulation show that blind policies generalize far better to unseen part shapes and sizes, though they can be slower. Training such policies needs thousands of different assemblies, each simulated with its clearance intact, so we also release an open-source generator that builds them procedurally from exact convex pieces for MuJoCo; it is more accurate and faster than convex decomposition or MuJoCo's signed-distance collision. Videos and interactive simulations are at https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/.
